title: Traffic thresholds, KPI conductor — preflight notes
content:
Purpose:
This note stitches together the traffic threshold guardrails, the KPI conductor matrix we will use for the pilot, and a compact preflight checklist for the 2-week beta ramp. The doc is intentionally lean — quick heuristics, explicit acceptance thresholds, and operator run-rates so on-call and ops teams can review quickly.

Context and intent:
- Pilot: Hosted API opt-in for 25 enterprise beta customers (limited features: batch embedding + text-gen v2).
- Goal: validate throughput economics (cost per 1k tokens) at live 95th-percentile latency <= 220ms for single-turn text-gen under 1k token requests.
- Timebox: 14 days, phased doubling traffic every 72 hours starting at 500 qps-min (synthetic + early customers).

KPI conductor (how we'll measure and act) — primary signals and ownership:
1) Latency SLOs (primary):
   - median p50, p95, p99 (ms) per route. Target: p95 <= 220ms, p99 <= 500ms. Owner: eng-serving-runtime + SRE.
   - action thresholds: amber when p95 > 220ms for 15m; red when p95 > 350ms for 5m.
2) Throughput and saturation:
   - GPU utilization per pool, request queue length, batch-size distribution. Target: avg GPU util 65–85% at steady-state. Owner: infra + dedicated ops.
3) Cost per 1k tokens (experimental):
   - rolling 24h: total infra cost / tokens served * 1000. Target: < $0.12/1k tokens for embeddings route; < $0.06/1k tokens for text-gen route (quantized model). Owner: finance + product-ops.
4) Quality regression watch (semantic):
   - eval set AUC + prompt-sample spot checks. Trigger: increase in semantic error rate > 2% vs baseline. Owner: research/quality.
5) Error budget and business signal:
   - customer-facing errors (5xx rate), degraded responses (timeouts). Budget: 0.5% allowed per day. Owner: product-ops + CS.

Traffic thresholds (ramp plan):
- Phase 0 (smoke): 500 qps-min synthetic, internal-only, 6 hours.
- Phase 1 (early): 2k qps for 72h with 3 pilot customers.
- Phase 2 (scale): 5k qps for 72h with 10 customers.
- Phase 3 (stress): 10–12k qps  for 48h parallel canary with burst policy enabled.
Stop/gate rules between phases (go/no-go):
- Gate if p95 > 300ms sustained for 30m OR 5xx rate > 1% for 15m OR GPU queue length > 2x baseline for 10m.
- If gate triggers, roll back traffic by 50% and trigger incident runbook.

Staffing & rotations (ops conductor):
- Daytime: 2x runtime engineers, 1x infra, 1x product-ops, 1x customer-success on standby (10:00–20:00 PT).
- Overnight: 1x on-call SRE + 1x runtime pager (20:00–10:00 PT).
- Escalation: pager -> duty lead -> eng manager -> CTO on red.
- Notes: staff overlap for first 48 hours of Phase 1 and Phase 2. Prepare handoff artifact with "what I did in last 4h" bullet summary.

Preflight checklist (quick run):
[ ] Canary config uploaded (IDs + traffic weights) — owner: release-engineering.
[ ] Model pin/version and rollback tag created — owner: product-hosted-api.
[ ] Key metrics dashboard (latency, queue, GPU util, 5xx) deployed with annotated thresholds — owner: observability.
[ ] Run synthetic soak for 6h with same customer payload distribution — owner: applied-ml.
[ ] Final runbook reviewed + incident contacts confirmed — owner: site-reliability-engineering.
[ ] Customer communications drafted (beta expectations + rollback notice) — owner: customer-success.

Acceptance criteria (explicit):
- Green: all key SLOs within target for 72h in Phase 1 and Phase 2; no more than one amber event that auto-resolved with scaling.
- Amber: any SLO breach that required manual intervention but contained within 2h.
- Red: persistent SLO breach > 2h or customer-facing outage > 5m.

Quick run heuristics and mitigations:
- If p95 climbs but GPU util low: suspect serialization or batching regression. Action: disable recent patch, increase batching window by +20ms, re-evaluate.
- If GPU util high and p95 high: scale pool by +30% capacity or enable burst capacity (Dedicated); if unavailable, reduce per-customer qps weights.
- If cost per 1k tokens spikes >25% from baseline: open cost incident, throttle embedding route non-critical customers, and enable cache prefixing.

Open questions / decisions to make:
- Do we allow per-customer burst beyond committed pool during Phase 3? (ops + sales tradeoff)
- Final cadence for quality spot-checks: hourly vs three-times-daily? (research input)
- Who authorizes cross-region fallback if US pool saturated? (requires legal on data residency)

Quick links and references:
- Throughput model (living): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/PPO/throughput-model-2024
- Rollout script (ops): https://github.com/redwood-inference/launch-scripts/pull/136
- Incident runbook: CONFLUENCE-RI-INCIDENT-03

Immediate next steps (this doc owner):
1) Lock staffing roster and circulate calendar invites by EOD (Maya).
2) Observability to finish dashboards and set alerts by +24h (Omar).
3) Finance to validate cost-per-token baseline and update sample calc workbook (Priya).
4) Draft customer beta email + rollback FAQs (Jonah).

Appendix — sample KPI calculation (text form):
- tokens_served_24h = sum(tokens per request in 24h window)
- infra_cost_24h = sum(GPU_hours * price_per_hour) + network + storage amortized
- cost_per_1k = (infra_cost_24h / tokens_served_24h) * 1000

Tone: operational, plain English, prioritized action items. This is a working doc — expect edits and comments.

Unresolved: add final list of pilot customers who have signed the data handling addendum (PD-DA) and the per-customer qps ceilings.
